notes:
• Apps and versions: one version and build number per application, kept by Devopper (all restart at 1.5.0)
• "Let Gramob find a driver later" closes the scheduled-ride request on the drivers (API, driver and passenger, Android and iOS) — when a passenger left Find a driver with "find a driver later", the "Scheduled ride request" dialog stayed up on the drivers it had been sent to. New POST passenger/rides/:id/find-later leaves the booking as it is, sends ride:scheduled_request_closed to every driver the request went to (except one re-confirming a moved time) and logs SCHEDULED_FIND_LATER; it returns {closed: 0} once the ride has a driver or is out to bidding. The driver apps close that ride's dialog, do not raise it again this session, and keep the ride on Requests to answer. The passenger apps call it on "find a driver later" and leave for Rides after the answer or after 4 seconds, whichever is first. New tests: find-later.spec.ts (API) and ScheduledRequestClosedTest (driver). iOS docs updated (api-contract, driver and passenger inventories). The API part needs a dev deploy; iOS not built here (no Xcode)
• Apps and versions: one version and build number per application, kept by Devopper (all restart at 1.5.0)
• Scheduled rides no longer clash (API, driver and passenger, Android and iOS) — a driver with a confirmed 12:30 scheduled ride could still offer on another 12:30 ride and kept getting ride-now requests, and the "Scheduled ride request" dialog was drawn over a live ride-now offer. The existing 60-minute clash window (now in schedule-clash.ts) is enforced everywhere: ride-now dispatch skips drivers holding a scheduled ride within the hour; a fare on a ride-now or an offer on a booking that clashes is refused (SCHEDULE_CLASH); a passenger choosing a driver who is now booked elsewhere is refused (DRIVER_SCHEDULE_CLASH) and that offer withdrawn; when a driver is given a booking their other clashing offers are withdrawn; clashing rides are left off the driver's Requests list and the passenger's offer list; and a passenger cannot book now or schedule within an hour of their own booking still waiting to go out (SCHEDULED_RIDE_CLASH; WhatsApp unchanged). The driver apps hold the scheduled-request dialog back while a ride-now offer is on screen and show it once that offer is answered or expires. New messages in English and Malayalam; iOS docs updated. API typecheck and tests pass (schedule-clash.spec.ts new), driver and passenger unit tests (ScheduleClashTest) and assembleRelease pass. Not yet tried on a phone; the API part needs a dev deploy. iOS not built here (no Xcode); version M2.0.233
• Driver app (Android and iOS): the ride request's "View & respond" sheet makes pickup, drop and the passenger stand out — the PICKUP and DROP labels are bold in their dot's colour (amber, green), the distance inside them ("278 m", "900 m") larger and extra bold, and the passenger's name larger and bold. The ride request ID is no longer shown at the top of the sheet. The scheduled-ride sheet on Requests gets the same labels. Driver unit tests and assembleRelease pass. Checked on the OPPO (release build, dev): labels, distances and name highlighted, no ride ID; the last version (distance without the tinted background) installed but not seen on screen. iOS not built here (no Xcode)
• Driver onboarding (Android and iOS): a required location consent under the Terms & Conditions tick — "I agree that Gramob may collect my location to send nearby ride requests and show my position to passengers, even when the app is closed or not in use." (English and Malayalam). Submit for verification goes ahead only with both ticks; without them each missing tick says so, and tapping the sentence ticks its box. The box sits by the first line of the text, in the Terms row's style. Driver unit tests, assembleDebug and assembleRelease pass. Tried on the OPPO (release build, dev) with a new test driver up to the review screen: both errors, the location error alone, ticking by the text, not submitted. Malayalam not viewed on screen; iOS not built here (no Xcode)
• Ride addresses stay in India, and the offer keypad is always whole (passenger and driver, Android and iOS) — a driver's offer showed the pickup "Seeroo IT Solutions, Đường Vân Nội, Phúc Thịnh": the right Kochi point, with a street near Hanoi from the passenger phone's own Geocoder, which takes no country. The passenger apps now drop a reverse-geocoded address outside India or more than 5 km from the pin (the nearest Google place or the pin's label names it instead), and geocoding a typed address into a point is kept to India (GeocodeCheck on Android, PlaceRules on iOS). On the driver's offer sheet the fare and its keypad no longer scroll with the ride's details, so 0 and delete are never below the fold under the countdown, and each address is cut to two lines. GeocodeCheckTest covers the rules; passenger and driver unit tests, assembleDebug and assembleRelease pass. iOS not built here (no Xcode). Installed on the OPPO, not yet tried on it; version M2.0.227
• Driver app: no location tracking straight after a reboot (Play compliance, Group 2 point 3) — after a reboot with the driver online, LocationServiceRestartReceiver no longer starts the location service; it posts a "Your phone restarted — Gramob Driver is not sharing your location. Tap to go online again." notice (English and Malayalam), and tracking starts only once the driver opens the app. A driver who was offline gets nothing. The restart alarm after the app is swiped away is unchanged, and scheduled-ride reminders are still re-armed after a reboot. The "tap to go online" notice is now taken down once tracking is back or the driver goes offline. RestartStepTest covers the boot/restart decision. Driver 100 unit tests, assembleDebug and assembleRelease pass. Tested on the OPPO (Android 15, release build): after a reboot no service ran, the notice appeared about a minute after unlock, and tapping it brought tracking and the online notice back. The offline-driver reboot was not run on a phone; version M2.0.226
